---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

internalId: f2ec9e28-8064-4707-bce9-b62f24d57524
---

# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor p

===== B_259_responsive_search_reopens_and_loses_results.md =====
---
id: B_259
internalId: e461b100-4b8f-435e-9c0f-81426d7fdb47
title: Responsive search reopens after Escape and loses results on resize
status: ready
agents:
  - design/releases/0.9.0/card__e461b100-4b8f-435e-9c0f-81426d7fdb47.json
changedFiles:
  - app/src/components/shell/search/search_control.test.tsx
---

Reported during review of [PR #27](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/27), head `e1181650a`. Fix after the PR is merged.

## Search reopens after Escape

1. Use a window width where search shows the shortcut presentation.
2. Open search by clicking its launcher.
3. Press Escape.

The popover closes and immediately reopens. Closing should dismiss search and leave keyboard navigation usable.

`SearchControl` uses a MUI `Popover` that restores focus to the launcher on close. `SearchLauncher` opens search through its `onFocus` handler, so restored focus opens it again. A targeted regression probe reproduced the failure; disabling focus restoration in a temporary probe prevented reopening.

Affected files: `app/src/components/shell/search/search_control.tsx` and `search_launcher.tsx`.

## Resizing clears results and search options

1. Open inline search and enter a query that returns a result, such as `Beta` in the existing test fixture.
2. Resize until search changes to a popover presentation.

The query remains, but the matching results disappear. RegExp mode and the background-body/action options also reset. Resizing should preserve the active search, its options, and matching results in either direction.

`SearchControl` mounts `SearchPanel` in separate inline and popover branches. Changing presentation remounts the panel. Only the query survives in `SearchControl`; `SearchPanel` initializes empty results and default options and does not apply its initial query on mount.

Affected files: `app/src/components/shell/search/search_control.tsx` and `search_panel.tsx`.

## Regression coverage

- Open shortcut search, press Escape, and verify it stays closed without preventing later reopening.
- Search for a matching card and resize between inline and popover presentations; verify the query and result remain available.
- Enable RegExp mode and background-body/action options before resizing; verify their selections and search behavior survive.

Both reported failures were reproduced with temporary probes in `search_control.test.tsx`; the probes were removed after review. No fix is included in this report.
===== B_260_source_indentation_lost_when_returning_to_rich_text.md =====
---
id: B_260
internalId: ef3c3a56-28a9-4ca5-9402-16972e140c01
title: Source indentation is lost when returning to Rich text
status: ready
after: 11011a61-0393-4aa1-9b89-f52be576aa72
agents:

  - app/src/components/editor/source/markdown_source_controller.ts
---

Reported during review of [PR #29](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/29), head `146ca4bb105c90cab3739d7f6356096608d6dfd8`. Fix after the PR is merged.

## Reproduction

1. Open a Markdown document containing `code` as an ordinary paragraph.
2. Switch to Source and add four leading spaces: `    code`.
3. Switch back to Rich text.
4. Add another paragraph and save.

Rich text still shows an ordinary paragraph instead of an indented code block. The subsequent rich edit exports `code` without its indentation, losing the Source change.

Expected: returning to Rich text imports the indented code block. Later edits, saving, and reopening preserve its code-block meaning; serialization may use a fenced code block.

## Cause and affected code

`MarkdownSourceController.setMode()` detects the Source change using exact comparison, but publishes `viewMode$` to let MDXEditor import it. MDXEditor's `setMarkdown$` compares trimmed strings and skips importing when only outer whitespace diffe

## Current state

Sibling create controls use `New â€¦` (`New card`, `New action`, `New diagram`). The sequence entry point still says `Add sequence` in:

* `app/src/components/shell/menu/app_menu.tsx` â€” desktop Home tab button (opens sequence popup via `handleOpenCardSequence`).
* `app/src/components/shell/menu/mobile_create_menu.tsx` â€” `Create` menu item (via `handleCreateSequence`).

Starting a sequence takes a long time. the `add sequence` popup also remains open long after it is visually clear that the first action already started.

This trace is from the renderer side: [Trace-renderer start sequence.json](file:///C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/Trace-renderer%20start%20sequence.json)

This trace is from the desktop app: [CPU-start sequence.cpuprofile](file:///C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/CPU-start%20sequence.cpuprofile)

The desktop app seems to do a lot of stuff. Meanwhile, the renderer seems to wait far too long.

What is the problem here? what is the sequence in the algorithm. how can we improve?

## Findings

The renderer waits for sequence registration, immediate activation, and a subsequent active-schedule refresh before closing the popup. Immediate activation includes worktree preparation, branch creation, schedule recovery writes, current-card context resolution, action startup, and initial conversation persistence. The popup does not need the result of those operations.

Registration also repeats work already represented by loaded application state:

* It loads the active-card project separately for every selected `cardInternalId` and validates card fields that are not required to persist the sequence.
* It resolves the action, validates agent settings, probes the executable, and loads the model catalog. Action execution performs the relevant resolution and executable check again.
* It performs a live worktree resolution. That resolution refreshes every linked worktree before revalidating the selected worktree. Sequence preparation and action execution repeat worktree resolution again.

The desktop CPU profile is mostly idle while it waits for filesystem operations and Git child processes. The delay is caused by synchronous orchestration and repeated I/O, not sustained CPU use.

## Revised registration flow

===== B_309_claude_questions_block_conversation_log.md =====
When claude asked a question and we answered, the conversation log stops showing any next messages. it seems the conversation log is in an incorrect state

## Current state

* `AgentRunnerService` owns the canonical `AgentConversation.entries` array. Streaming assistant and provider-event updates carry their exact backend `entryIndex`; `ActionRunRegistry` applies each update at that index and rejects an identity or sequence mismatch.
* Since commit `0d18f34d7e5326d915637f74187e8342cd80df1a` on 2026-09-06, `handleQuestion` appends an `agentQuestion` event to the backend conversation. This entry persists the pending questions so they can be restored after restart.
* The live question notification does not send that transcript entry. `ActionRun` publishes an `agentQuestion` update containing only questions and request id, and `ActionRunRegistry` only sets the question box. Its live conversation therefore becomes one entry shorter than the backend conversation.
* Answering appends the answer message on both sides but does not repair that offset. The next backend `agentOutput` index is one greater than the renderer's append position. `updateAgentOutputAtIndex` rejects it; since commit `2cc2a439d06756c778e8c6bfaa19f05a27987d5c` on 2026-10-08, the registry catches the error, logs `[action:agentOutput]`, and drops the conversation update. Every later indexed update remains offset, so the live conversation appears frozen while Claude and the backend continue.
* `ActionConversationChatlogTracker` already hides `agentQuestion` transcript events because the question box is their visible UI. Keeping the hidden entry in the live conversation will preserve index alignment without adding a duplicate row.
* Claude's streamed and aggregated text reconciliation already has focused `AskUserQuestion` coverage. It is not the failing layer.

## implementation details

* Change `appendQuestionEntry` in `agent_streaming_event_handlers.js` to return the created event and its index after appending it to `run.conversation.entries`.
* For a newly received live question, keep checkpoint persistence first. After persistence succeeds, emit the returned entry through the existing `{ entryIndex, event, type: 'agentEvent' }` path before publishing the `question` update. `ActionRun` and `ActionRunRegistry` already forward and apply this granular transcript update; no new update type is needed.
* Do not emit another transcript entry when `handleSessionReady` restores a pending question. The `agentStarted` conversation snapshot already contains its persisted `agentQuestion` entry; `sessionReady` should only restore the question box.
* Keep `conversationEventIsVisible` unchanged so `agentQuestion` remains hidden from the transcript. Keep strict index, message identity, and sequence validation unchanged; they correctly expose backend-renderer divergence.
* This uses the generic agent-question path and therefore fixes any provider that sends a structured live question, including Claude. Do not change Claude stream correlation, answer submission, dismissal, status transitions, or conversation identity.
* Add `agent_runner_state.test.mjs` coverage asserting that a new question emits one indexed `agentEvent` matching the entry persisted in the backend conversation.
* Add `action_run_registry.node.test.ts` regression sequences for question then answer then assistant output, and question then dismissal then assistant output. Assert backend indexes append successfully and later messages remain in the live conversation.
* Keep or extend chatlog tracker coverage proving `agentQuestion` exists in canonical entries but renders no transcript row. Add restored-question coverage proving `sessionReady` does not duplicate the entry.

## acceptance criteria

* Backend and live renderer conversations contain the same ordered entries and indexes throughout a live question, answer, or dismissal.
* After a user answers or dismisses a live Claude question, every later assistant mess

entries.content:
md² appears eligible, but I recommend submitting it under **Agent Infrastructure → Multi-Agent Orchestration**, not **AI-Native IDEs**.

The IDE category is defined as full development environments offering code generation, chat, and debugging. md² is positioned as an orchestration workspace around Codex CLI and Claude Code, Markdown feature cards, and isolated Git worktrees. That closely matches existing entries such as Conductor, Vibe Kanban, and Kagan. [See the list’s categories](https://github.com/jamesmurdza/awesome-ai-devtools#multi-agent-orchestration).

### What to do

1. Fork `jamesmurdza/awesome-ai-devtools`.
2. Add one entry to `README.md` under `### Multi-Agent Orchestration`.
3. Open a pull request titled:
   `Add md² to Multi-Agent Orchestration`
4. Complete the repository’s checklist:
   - The tool uses AI.
   - It is developer-focused.
   - The description is clear and unambiguous.
   - The description matches other entries’ style.

Those are the only published submission requirements. Self-submissions are not prohibited. [Contribution rules](https://github.com/jamesmurdza/awesome-ai-devtools/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).

### Suggested entry

```markdown
* [md²](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2) — Open-source Electron workspace for planning, running, and tracking Codex CLI and Claude Code tasks from local Markdown cards. Runs coding agents in parallel Git worktrees with a Kanban-style dashboard, conversation history, merge workflows, reusable actions, diagrams, and token and cost tracking.
```

This description is supported by the current [md² README](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2), including the downloadable Windows installer, agent integrations, worktree management, and documentation.

### Suggested PR description

```markdown
## Description

Adds md² to Multi-Agent Orchestration.

md² is an open-source Electron workspace for managing Codex CLI and Claude Code work by feature. It can run coding agents in parallel Git worktrees and connects their conversations, commits, resource usage, and merge workflow to local Markdown cards.

## Checklist

- [x] The entry is a tool that uses AI
- [x] The entry is a developer-focused tool
- [x] The description is unambiguous and clear
- [x] The description matches the style of other entries
```

I would not submit it under AI-Native IDEs unless md² is intentionally repositioned as a complete IDE with built-in source editing and debugging. The orchestration category is a much stronger, more defensible fit and therefore likelier to be accepted.

import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'
import type { ActionContext } from '../../../../data/action_context'
import type { ActionDefinition } from '../../../../data/action_types'
import type { ActionPromptDraft } from '../../../../services/actions/action_prompt_draft_service'
import { ActionSchedulePopover } from './action_schedule_popover'
import type { ActionScheduleStore } from './action_schedule_store'

interface ActionScheduleOwnerProps {
    accountId?: string
    action: ActionDefinition
    conversationId: string | null
    context: ActionContext
    promptDraft: ActionPromptDraft
    selectionValidationError?: string | null
    store: ActionScheduleStore
}

/** Mounts the schedule popover and its project-data consumers only while scheduling is open. */
export function ActionScheduleOwner(props: ActionScheduleOwnerProps) {
    const { store } = props
    const open = useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, store.getOpenSnapshot, store.getOpenSnapshot)
    if (!open) return null

    return <ActionSchedulePopover {...props} />
}

import { DIAGRAM_DATA_VERSION, type DiagramData, type DiagramFlowPreset, type DiagramType } from './diagram_data'

export type EmptyDiagramChoiceId = 'architecture' | 'dependency' | 'entity' | 'flowchart' | 'mindmap' | 'sequence' | 'state'

export interface EmptyDiagramChoice {
    description: string
    id: EmptyDiagramChoiceId
    label: string
    preset?: DiagramFlowPreset
    title: string
    type: DiagramType
}

export const EMPTY_DIAGRAM_CHOICES: readonly EmptyDiagramChoice[] = [
    { description: 'New architecture diagram', id: 'architecture', label: 'Architecture', title: 'New architecture', type: 'architecture' },
    { description: 'New dependency diagram', id: 'dependency', label: 'Dependency', title: 'New dependency', type: 'dependency' },
    { description: 'New sequence diagram', id: 'sequence', label: 'Sequence', title: 'New sequence', type: 'sequence' },
    { description: 'New flowchart diagram', id: 'flowchart', label: 'Flowchart', preset: 'flowchart', title: 'New flowchart', type: 'flow' },
    { description: 'New state diagram', id: 'state', label: 'State diagram', preset: 'state', title: 'New state diagram', type: 'flow' },
    { description: 'New entity diagram', id: 'entity', label: 'Entity', title: 'New entity', type: 'entity' },
    { description: 'New mindmap diagram', id: 'mindmap', label: 'Mindmap', title: 'New mindmap', type: 'mindmap' },
]

/** Builds canonical persisted data for a new empty diagram. */
export function createEmptyDiagramData(choice: EmptyDiagramChoice): DiagramData {
    return {
        edges: [],
        groups: [],
        meta: {
            description: choice.description,
            legend: [],
            ...(choice.preset ? { preset: choice.preset } : {}),
            title: choice.title,
            type: choice.type,
            version: DIAGRAM_DATA_VERSION,
        },
        nodes: [],
    }
}
import type { DiagramData, DiagramEdge, DiagramLegendEntryData, DiagramNode } from './diagram_data'
import { diagramEdgeKindLabel, diagramNodeKindLabel, effectiveDiagramNodeKind } from './diagram_creation_tool_labels'

/** Derives distinct node kinds and connection kinds in first-appearance order. */
export function derivedDiagramLegendEntries(data: {
    meta: Pick<DiagramData['meta'], 'type'>
    nodes: readonly Pick<DiagramNode, 'kind' | 'role'>[]
    edges: readonly Pick<DiagramEdge, 'kind'>[]
}): DiagramLegendEntryData[] {
    const nodeKinds = [...new Set(data.nodes.map(({ kind }) => effectiveDiagramNodeKind(kind, data.meta.type)))]
    const edgeKinds = [...new Set(data.edges.map(({ kind }) => kind))]

    return [
        ...nodeKinds.map((nodeKind, index) => ({ id: `derived-legend-${index + 1}`, label: diagramNodeKindLabel(nodeKind), nodeKind })),
        ...edgeKinds.map((kind, index) => ({ id: `derived-legend-${nodeKinds.length + index + 1}`, kind, label: diagramEdgeKindLabel(kind) })),
    ]
}

describe('overlay lifecycle', () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
        vi.spyOn(dataService, 'getState').mockReturnValue({
            project: { branch: 'main', id: 'project', rootPath: 'C:\\project' },
            runningAgents: [],
            snapshot: { activeCards: [card], backgroundCards: [], repositoryFiles: [], workingFolder: 'design' },
        })
    })

    afterEach(() => {
        cleanup()
        vi.restoreAllMocks()
    })

    it('mounts only open card overlays and removes them when closed', () => {
        renderCard()

        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-menu')).not.toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-card-archive-dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-card-delete-dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument()

        fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Card actions for F-1' }))
        expect(screen.getByTestId('mounted-menu')).toBeInTheDocument()
        fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Archive' }))

        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-menu')).not.toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.getByTestId('mounted-card-archive-dialog')).toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-card-delete-dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument()

        fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Close archive dialog' }))
        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-card-archive-dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument()
    })

    it('mounts only open worktree overlay and removes it when closed', () => {
        renderWorktreeSelector()

        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-menu')).not.toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-worktree-commit-dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-worktree-integration-dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument()
        expect(screen.queryByTestId('mounted-worktree-unassign-dialog')).not.toBeInTheDocument()

        fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /F-1: C:\\feature/u }))

import { useCallback, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'
import type { ActionContext } from '../../../../data/action_context'
import {
    CARD_ADDED_EVENT,
    CARD_REMOVED_EVENT,
    cardCollectionFieldChangedEvent,
    dataService,
} from '../../../../services/data/data_service'

const TARGET_EVENTS = [
    cardCollectionFieldChangedEvent('identity'),
    cardCollectionFieldChangedEvent('title'),
    CARD_ADDED_EVENT,
    CARD_REMOVED_EVENT,
]

function findTargetCard(cardInternalId: string) {
    const snapshot = dataService.getState().snapshot
    const cards = [...(snapshot?.activeCards ?? []), ...(snapshot?.backgroundCards ?? [])]

    return cards.find(({ header }) => header.internalId === cardInternalId) ?? null
}

function subscribeTargetEvents(listener: () => void) {
    TARGET_EVENTS.forEach((eventName) => dataService.addEventListener(eventName, listener))

    return () => TARGET_EVENTS.forEach((eventName) => dataService.removeEventListener(eventName, listener))
}

function subscribeNothing() {
    return () => undefined
}

/**
 * Badge id plus tooltip title, resolved by canonical card identity. The title follows a card renamed
 * while the popup stays open and falls back to the title captured in the context.
 */
export function usePopupTarget(context: ActionContext) {
    const cardInternalId = context.kind === 'card' ? context.cardInternalId ?? null : null
    const subscribe = cardInternalId ? subscribeTargetEvents : subscribeNothing
    const getId = useCallback(() => cardInternalId ? findTargetCard(cardInternalId)?.header.id ?? null : null, [cardInternalId])
    const getTitle = useCallback(() => cardInternalId ? findTargetCard(cardInternalId)?.header.title ?? null : null, [cardInternalId])
    const id = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getId, getId)
    const title = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getTitle, getTitle)
    if (context.kind === 'project') return { id: 'Project', title: null }
    if (context.kind !== 'card') return { id: null, title: null }

    return { id, title: title ?? context.title ?? null }
}
